study: Full CUDA 11.8 qualification of stronger Legendre baselines
dispatch: One exact-handle owned GPU child at a time. Run the serial observer before its matched warp observer. Record actual dependency closure, CUDA 11.8 DLL hashes, CUDA source and raw CPU/GPU state/probe hashes. Stop the cohort on the first numerical or transport anomaly. No fused nonlinear kernel or newer CUDA runtime in this numerical cohort.

watchdog.policy: Wait on the original Popen process handle, never on a reused PID. Timeout may terminate only that handle. If cleanup is unconfirmed, do not launch another child or reset the GPU.

cpu_evidence: Keep the original four-case exploratory and supplemental rank40 records and the four-case fair switch archive. All GPU comparisons use each new configuration's own same-schedule CPU states and probes. No reuse of the larger Legendre37/39 qualifications. Legendre33/K72 remains an accuracy failure control only.
uniform_observations: All 19 absolute physical checkpoints and 577 full-horizon probes. Match the same-space r128 or r152 CPU anchor on all four field norms and both probe types.
combined_observations: Also save the two actual bridge instants t8+1/late_rate and t8+2/late_rate. CPU implementation comparison covers all 21 times. Physical and triangle checks cover only the original 19. The triangle uses the new configuration's own same-space uniform CPU anchor.
warp_scope: In addition to the common CPU, physical and wake gates, compare the paired serial GPU state, times and probe times byte-for-byte. Compare both complete probe histories with relative L2 and pointwise max abs(delta)/max(1,abs(serial)), each at most 1e-12. The serial and warp outcomes remain separate; neither can inherit qualification from the other.
timing_scope: Accuracy only. No speed ranking, no toolkit or fusion extrapolation. Future timed tuple must qualify at the final engine, observer, rank, and schedule before it is eligible.
